ai.description: *Ichthyophis tricolor* reaches 30–40 cm. It is dark violet-brown with a distinct yellow lateral stripe and a yellow-spotted underside. It features a blunt snout and 300–350 primary annular grooves.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ichthyophis tricolor* is uniquely distinguished by a distinct, continuous yellow lateral stripe that runs along its entire body, separating it from other Indian species.
ai.habitat: *Ichthyophis tricolor* inhabits moist, evergreen tropical forests and plantations in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 500 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Maddatorai caecilian is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows at night to forage for earthworms and other small invertebrates in moist soil.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ichthyophis tricolor* is oviparous, laying clutches of 20–50 eggs in underground burrows during the monsoon season. Females exhibit maternal care by guarding the eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ichthyophis tricolor* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 300 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Maddatorai Caecilian produces a faint, high-pitched, rhythmic clicking sound, typically emitted from within saturated soil or shallow burrows near forest streams.
